text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: continuous-batching-service experiencing elevated p95 latency and request queueing in us-west-2. Alert history: incrementing for 6m. Affected customer traffic on model: redwood/open-ev-v2 and fallback variants.
Maya K: I'm on it, grabbing graphs. Can someone check KV cache metrics (entries, evictions) and current microbatch window?
Samir P: KV cache entries spiked ~30x around 18:02 UTC, eviction rate low. Looks like cache misses skyrocketed leading to larger prefix loads.
Ravi: Observed sudden increase in continuous_batching.max_microbatch (someone rolled out change) — controller shows window=2048 for some pods.
Lena: oof that explains it. Larger microbatch + high concurrency = queueing + big KV pulls.
ops-sre: Confirming: router queue length jumped >2000, downstream worker CPU pinned, multiple pods reporting GC pressure.
Maya K: @Ravi can you pull the rollout history? Who rolled that flag?
Ravi: Patchset by infra-team yesterday 03:15 prod deploy. Hash: a7c3f2.
Samir P: Customer impact estimate: ~6% of requests had >10s tail, ~0.7% 5xx errors due to timeouts. Impact centered on high-concurrency routes (chat and streaming).
pagerduty-bot: Incident severity: S2 auto. Trigger: continuous_batching_p95>1.5s AND queue_length>1000.
Maya K: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) roll back microbatch window to 512 on affected pods 2) enable kv_cache.eviction_boost=1.0 for 10m 3) scale workers by +20% to drain queue.
Lena: I'll push rollback to canary first, then prod. Doing: 
```bash
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/continuous-batcher CONTINUOUS_MAX_MICROBATCH=512 --record
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/continuous-batcher
```
Maya K: Samir, can you toggle eviction boost via runtime flags?
Samir P: On it, patching feature flags service: 
```json
{"kv_cache": {"eviction_boost": 1.0, "sampling_window_sec": 30}}
```
Samir P: Pushed. logs: eviction_rate increased, entries trending down after 45s.
Ravi: Starting scale-up: autoscaler temporary override to +20% for batchers.
ops-sre: Scale applied. New pods coming up, but note: some older pods still hold large KV caches; eviction will clear them gradually.
Maya K: We're seeing p95 drop from 2.3s -> 1.1s in the canary after rollback. Prod trending similar. Queue length decreasing.
Lena: Rolling the rollback across remaining zones. Noticing one pod stuck Terminating on restart (oom?). Investigating.
Ravi: That pod had huge resident memory (12GB for cache). I'll cordon and force-deploy replacement.
ops-sre: Forced replacement succeeded. New pod started healthy.
Maya K: After mitigation: overall p95 ~0.9s, 5xx rate back to baseline. Customer-facing errors reduced.
Samir P: Quick root-cause hypothesis: inadvertent increase of microbatch window combined with high concurrency load changed KV cache working set -> eviction rate too-low -> cache blowup -> heavy I/O to fetch cold prefixes -> latency cliff. Also lack of jitter increased synchronized microbatching which amplified peaks.
Lena: Immediate follow-ups (tickets):
- RWD-INC-3241: Revert/lock microbatch default at 512 and add rollout guard (ops-approved flag). Assignee: infra-team.
- RWD-INC-3242: Improve KV cache observability (per-pod cache size metric + alert when >2x baseline). Assignee: eng-runtime.
- RWD-INC-3243: Add jitter/randomization (microbatch start jitter) in continuous batching to prevent sync waves. Assignee: runtime-team.
- RWD-INC-3244: Postmortem and customer impact email draft. Assignee: Maya.
Maya K: Customers impacted: 2 mid-market tenants reported higher latency in monitoring during window — CS notified and one ticket opened. No data exfiltration or model quality regressions.
Samir P: Note for follow-up: Add canary gating on continuous_batching.max_microbatch change (runtime config PRs should not exceed 1024 without infra approval).
Ravi: Also propose a temporary circuit-breaker: if queue_length>1500 then force-reduce per-pod microbatch to 256 to protect latency. Will prototype.
ops-sre: Logging: captured stack traces from one overloaded worker, saved in /var/log/continuous-batch/stack-1810009999.log and uploaded to s3://redwood-ops-incident/1810009999/
Maya K: Handoff notes as we move to steady state: 
- Mitigations applied: rollback microbatch -> 512, eviction_boost enabled, +20% worker scale, restart unhealthy pods.
- Current status: p95 stable ~0.85-1.0s, queue draining, no active customer-facing errors.
- Next steps: infra to lock config, runtime to add jitter and eviction metrics, ops to follow postmortem.
Lena: I'll start the postmortem doc and tag owners. Draft link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RWD-INC-3244 (placeholder).
Maya K: Thanks all. If anything regresses, re-alert and we'll re-escalate. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident closed (auto) after 45m of stable metrics.
